system.description:
The wall-knight who holds what others attack. Examples: the Boldock Wall-Knights facing the Red Waste from the Wall and Westfront Fort, and the keepers of every border hold.

  • Shield of the Wall (1st): you guard a steady ally and hold the line beside it.
    • Guard: choose an ally within 30ft of you that hasn't moved since the start of its last turn: the first attack against it each round has Disadvantage.
    • Hold the Wall: while an ally is within 5ft of you, you and that ally have Advantage on checks to resist being shoved, tripped or grappled.
  • Siege Discipline (1st): Advantage on checks involving fortification, siege assessment or coordinating a defence.
  • Wall-Forged Dread (5th): you gain Demoralise at 5th level rather than 7th.
    • 7th level: an enemy Frightened by your Demoralise also can't willingly move closer to the ally you guard with Shield of the Wall.
  • Keeper of the Gate (10th): garrisons, watch-houses and border forts treat you as one of their own: a bed, a hearing with the commander and the wall's news for the asking. Once you've stood a watch with them, a commander lends you 1d4 guards for a day's errand.

features.name: Wall-Forged Dread
features.description: You gain Demoralise at 5th level rather than 7th, and it is harsher: on a failed Will save, enemies stay Frightened of you while the Command lasts, not just until the end of their next turn. When you give Demoralise, apply this in place of the usual failed-save effect.
